headline: Singapore's central bank links AI investment to above-trend growth and forecasts a 2027 moderation
summary: In its 14 October 2026 Macroeconomic Review, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said robust global investment in AI is buoying Singapore's above-trend expansion and that AI-related production backlogs and capacity additions should support near-term growth. MAS expects technology-sector activity to moderate in 2027 from an exceptional 2026 pace while remaining the principal growth driver. The same-day advance GDP release reports Q3 growth of 5.4% year on year and 1.1% quarter on quarter, easing from revised Q2 growth of 6.2% and 1.5%, respectively; manufacturing grew 7.5% year on year, with mixed quarter-on-quarter performance. SingStat says the Q3 estimate is based mainly on July–August data and may be revised. These figures do not isolate AI's contribution. MAS's policy statement separately links global AI investment to regional production and trade and flags a sharper investment pullback as a risk; this remains an official assessment, not an independent causal estimate.
